paragraphs: Prepared builds assistive artificial intelligence for 911 centers, aimed at the people who answer emergency calls and send help. The company states that it is now the intelligence layer of Axon 911, an emergency communications platform it describes as covering the full lifecycle of a call.

During a call the software transcribes speech as it happens, captures details automatically, and translates, so staff can watch the caller rather than the keyboard. Incoming audio is translated automatically in more than 40 languages, according to the homepage. The call-taking page claims support for over 200 languages for callers who do not speak English. Call-takers can also request a livestream from the caller to see the scene. A separate voice assistant answers non-emergency lines and converses with callers in English or Spanish.

Buyers are public safety answering points, the centers that take 911 calls. Prepared describes the product as a cloud based platform laid over existing systems, with no rip and replace required. Supervisors get automated quality assurance and keyword triggers for visibility into the operation. Its chief executive, Michael Chime, appears in a recorded discussion with three 911 leaders about non-emergency calls.

quote.text: Assistive intelligence, built for the people on the headset.
